lesson_title: Where the Slide Meets the Ladder
hook_text: Nobody sets the price of a muffin. So how does the market find R12?
clip_script: Learners want lots of muffins when they are cheap. That is the demand slide. Bakers make lots when the price is high. That is the supply ladder. Put them on one graph and they cross at one point: R12 and 120 muffins. Every muffin baked is sold, everyone willing to pay R12 gets one. That is equilibrium. Now get the price wrong. Charge R16: bakers make 160, learners buy 80, and 80 stale muffins are left. The price drops. Charge R8: 170 learners want one, only 80 are baked, and the queue is out the door. The price rises. Either way, the market drags itself back to R12. Then a new school opens next door. Demand jumps, a queue forms at R12, and the new meeting point is R16 and 160 muffins. Nobody planned it. Everyone just reacted. That is the price mechanism.
visual_style: A playground slide and a ladder morphing into D and S curves that cross at a glowing point E; piles of stale muffins and a long queue appearing on either side; the slide shifting right with a new school.
mood: Playful, then a satisfying click into balance.
pacing: Quick setup, a dramatic wrong-price beat, a firm return to R12, a lively shift finale.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and work out the four moves of demand and supply.
